title: Markdown to PDF: a practical guide for readable documents
description: Prepare a clear Markdown source, convert it to PDF, and review tables, code, headings and page breaks before sharing it.
author: AI SmartTalk
article_markdown:
Markdown keeps content separate from presentation. That makes it useful for reports, technical notes and proposals that may need to appear in more than one format. When you need to send the result to a customer or attach it to a case file, PDF is still a convenient format to read and share.

This guide walks through a simple Markdown to PDF workflow and the checks that matter when the document is generated repeatedly.

## 1. Give the document a clear structure

Use one main title, followed by sections in a logical order. Avoid jumping from a level-two heading straight to level four: heading levels should describe the structure of the document. Short paragraphs and lists also make a PDF easier to scan on screen.

```markdown
# Monthly report

## Summary

The main results for this month.

## Next steps

- Confirm the figures with the team.
- Prepare the next review.
```

## 2. Review elements that cross page boundaries

Wide tables, long code samples and images are the elements most likely to run into the page margin or split awkwardly. Before sharing a document, check that each table fits the page width, code remains readable, links point to the right resources, headings are not stranded at the bottom of a page, and the last page contains the expected content.

When a table has many columns, shorten the labels or split the data into two tables. Landscape orientation can help, but it does not replace a clear structure.

## 3. Create a first PDF

For a quick conversion, [open the Markdown to PDF tool](/en/markdown-to-pdf), paste your document and download the result. The page sends the PDF straight back to your browser and is designed for manual trials.

To call the service from a program, the API accepts JSON and returns a PDF:

```bash
curl https://pdf.aismarttalk.tech/api/convert \
  -H "X-API-Key: $MDTOPDF_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"markdown":"# Report\n\nMonthly results."}' \
  --output report.pdf
```

Keep the API key in a server-side secrets manager. Do not put it in JavaScript delivered to a browser. The [PDF API page](/en/pdf-generation-api) describes the input formats and available tools.

## 4. When to use a template

A Markdown file works well when the structure changes from one document to another. If you repeatedly create the same report with different names, dates and metrics, separate the structure from the data: an HTML template and a JSON object are easier to maintain than a long string assembled in application code. Versioned themes can then share colours and typography across renders.

## 5. Keep an output review step

A successful response confirms that the service produced a file; it does not confirm that every page matches your intent. Open the PDF and inspect the actual output when the document matters. The API also offers PNG previews and a layout analysis that can identify some overflows, split tables and orphaned headings.

A useful rule is to automate repetitive generation while keeping review proportional to the document's risk. A quick preview may be enough for an internal note. For a customer-facing document, also verify the data, links and template version.
